toolDescriptions.name: twin__describe
toolDescriptions.description: What the twin is: the model in one paragraph, the files it was built from with their sha256, the thresholds, the budget of a question.

toolDescriptions.name: twin__time_to_critical
toolDescriptions.description: How the cabin CO2 evolves from a starting state at a scrubber flow, with an optional stop: the minutes until ELEVATED and until CRITICAL, the peak, the final state, the energy the scrubber draws. Defaults come from the scenario's start (four asleep, 1500 ppm, 33 %). Use stopMinutes to ask 'what if the scrubber stops now for that long': it is powered off and draws nothing for those minutes, then restarts at resumePercent, and removes nothing during its restart latency (the answer says how long) before the usual lag.

toolDescriptions.name: twin__habitat_run
toolDescriptions.description: The station's reference twin (the library's habitat graph: the Lab and Hab-B in mass, the centralised scrubber, the inter-module ventilation through its filter, the persons by name) run for some minutes at a scrubber command, with an optional stop. Who is on board is given person by person (module and activity: the medical monitor's presence, or a what-if), the scrubber's own numbers from the register's devices, the installation's numbers as a commissioning fitted them (variables); each takes the reference's default when absent, and the answer says what it took by default. Per module: the peak, the final CO2, the minutes to ELEVATED and to CRITICAL, the curve every few minutes; what the ventilation delivered and what the scrubber removed.

toolDescriptions.name: twin__sweep
toolDescriptions.description: The operating map: for each scrubber flow in a list, run the twin from a starting state with a crew for some minutes and report the peak, the final state, the minutes to ELEVATED and CRITICAL, the steady state and the energy drawn. A few points under the budget; a full grid is a factory job.

toolDescriptions.description: Check required validation, admission and installed-twin services. Mother explicitly reports missing capabilities or missing commander holders; this does not finish a mission.

toolDescriptions.name: station__twin_validate
toolDescriptions.description: Request independent validation of a received graph proposal for a registered device. Requires telemetry in a separate hashed validation task, bound to the same device. Replays the exact candidate without fitting; Mother reports failures. This does not install anything.

toolDescriptions.name: station__twin_admit
toolDescriptions.description: Ask the authorised commander to install an independently validated twin for its exact device. Opens a real question in Mother's chat. The station installs only after the answer; the supervisor cannot approve its own request.

toolDescriptions.name: station__twin_state
toolDescriptions.description: Read the real active installation for a registered device, its independent report and whether its descriptor still matches. Empty means not installed, even if a reference simulation runs.

toolDescriptions.name: station__twin_run
toolDescriptions.description: Consult the twin actually installed for a registered device. Refuses missing or stale installation, executes its exact graph and returns provenance with the result. This is distinct from the reference habitat twin.

toolDescriptions.name: station__proposals
toolDescriptions.description: Read the artifact proposals received by the station, including their provenance and current status. Received or proposed does not mean validated or installed.

toolDescriptions.name: station__register_artifact
toolDescriptions.description: Register a monitor artifact for push. Refused without the id of a positive evaluate report (the three locks of the design document).

toolDescriptions.name: station__diagnostic_load_model
toolDescriptions.description: Push a registered artifact to a device (validated: the device checks sha256 and contract). Refused for an unregistered sha256.

toolDescriptions.name: station__journal_rows
toolDescriptions.description: Rows of the journal of stable operating points, in the shape the fit job reads (duty_percent, current_amps). Stub: empty until a device sends operating_point notifications.

toolDescriptions.name: station__registry_list
toolDescriptions.description: Every device on the register: its ISA-95 path, its descriptor (type, title, properties with quantity and unit, actions, links), whether a qualified simulator exists for it, and the last readings it reported. Reading is free.

toolDescriptions.name: station__operation_request
toolDescriptions.description: Proposes an operation on a life-support device to the commander: what to run and with what input, why, the conditions it rests on (safeguards, recovery, what to watch), and the evidence read for it (tool answers, documents). Nothing runs now: the commander authorises or refuses; if authorised, the station runs it, and the device's own guard accepts or refuses it. Read the decision and the device's answer with station.operations. Operations: scrubber.stop { minutes }, scrubber.set_speed { percent }.

toolDescriptions.name: station__operations
toolDescriptions.description: The operations agents asked for on life-support devices: each with its status (pending, refused by the commander, executed, refused by the device), the commander's decision and what the device answered. One by its requestId, or all.

toolDescriptions.name: station__commissioning_state
toolDescriptions.description: One commissioning by its id, or all of them: the device, the status (open, awaiting-authorisation, authorised, refused, running, done, aborted), the procedures checked, the procedure relayed with who is in the volume, the authorisation, the monitoring session, the steps run and the report. Reading is free.

toolDescriptions.name: factory__request
toolDescriptions.description: Use topics ["procedure"] to request a test procedure: provide the quantities to identify, target device in observations.device, observed operating limits and available evidence in the functional contract. The procedure builder proposes an artifact; the station checks it and opens its own commander authorisation question. No calibration telemetry is required to write a procedure. Use ["graph"] to construct a twin from recorded telemetry, ["onnx"] for a learned model, or another declared topic for that work. The caller chooses the topic; this tool does not infer a recovery workflow or execute hardware. The functional contract of what you lack: the outputs a plan must produce (name, quantity, unit, horizon), the constraints (a residual threshold and its window), what you observed (volumes, door, occupancy, scrubbers), the data available (telemetry files with their columns), the topics and a budget. The factory opens a workspace, writes the task file and the data you hand it (rows or text, with their sha256), returns the task id and starts its loop on the task at once (run: false only opens the task); the loop ends by proposing to the station, which asks the twin's judgment. Ask for the need, never for a solution; follow the task with `task`.

toolDescriptions.name: factory__start
toolDescriptions.description: Execute an existing unstarted task, including one forwarded by the Observer. Creation alone does not run a task. Refuses tasks already launched or ended. This starts factory work, never physical hardware or artifact installation.

toolDescriptions.name: factory__task
toolDescriptions.description: The state of a factory task (created, running, done, proposed, accepted, rejected, failed), its workspace, the sha256 of its task file, how many files it holds, its manifest when the loop has written one (every step with its source, outcome, reward and reason; the artifacts with their sha256; the proposal), and, while the loop runs here, the builder and the last stage reached. Includes the selected topic and inputStatus: a ready procedure task is distinct from a graph task blocked on telemetry.

toolDescriptions.name: factory__inventory
toolDescriptions.description: The inventory of the installation, read from the station's register through the broker: every device with its ISA-95 path, what it is, what it measures and in which unit, what it accepts; the volumes of air (the places that hold a CO2 sensor), the openings between them (a device that declares it connects two places), which device is being commissioned, and what the register does not say (the served volume, measured; the exchange through an opening, a hypothesis).

toolDescriptions.name: agent__procedure_execute
toolDescriptions.description: Request execution of an existing checked procedure after an actual commander authorisation. The deterministic executor sends the approved steps through the agent's own broker rights and checks every abort condition. Returns a runId immediately; results return to the same mission. Current logger: simulated Lab cabin, driven by observed device speed, hatch closed. Does not invent physical CO2 measurements.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__procedure_result
toolDescriptions.description: Read an authorised procedure's actual execution result, logged telemetry, device descriptors, presence and report. Factory requests can name this runId as telemetryRunId to copy its recorded data without manual transcription.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__describe
toolDescriptions.description: The provider and its family, the guard, how many capabilities the agent may reach, the scenario it plays and its events, and where it stands.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__state
toolDescriptions.description: The mode (idle, playing, paused, ended), the event being played with its minute, the step inside it, and the last decision.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__reset
toolDescriptions.description: Puts the board back where the scenario starts, rebuilds the agent so it has learned nothing, and returns to the first event. Stops a run in progress.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__next
toolDescriptions.description: Takes one decision and stops. Enters the next event of the night when the agent hands the console back or the step cap is reached.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__play
toolDescriptions.description: Takes decisions on its own, about one a second, until pause, stop, or the end of the night. With an intention, jumps to that event of the night first and plays from there. Returns at once; watch the event log or call state.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__pause
toolDescriptions.description: The decision under way finishes; the next one is not taken. `play` or `next` goes on from there.

toolDescriptions.name: agent__stop
toolDescriptions.description: Leaves the night where it is and returns to idle. The board is not touched: use reset for that.

toolDescriptions.name: speech__say
toolDescriptions.description: Say a short message aloud to the crew or operator. Mother (station voice) finishes her current sentence, then plays only her newest pending message; superseded messages remain in the written history. Other voices retain queue order. One or two sentences in the listener's language, with the numbers you were given. Returns an utterance identifier, never the audio.

toolDescriptions.name: speech__stop
toolDescriptions.description: Stop the audio outputs: one utterance by its identifier, or everything queued so far.

toolDescriptions.name: biomed__describe
toolDescriptions.description: The biomed monitor: the roster, the nominal band, the source behind the readings, and whether a monitoring session is open (none between tests: the station opens one when the commander authorises a test, for the subjects the procedure names). Says plainly when the readings are simulated.

toolDescriptions.name: biomed__presence
toolDescriptions.description: Who is aboard: the occupants of every module and what each one is doing now (sleep, rest, light_work, heavy_work, or unknown). The crew's activity is where the cabin's CO2 load comes from; the occupants are who a change of the air, or a test on a volume, exposes, and therefore why a human has to authorise it.

toolDescriptions.name: biomed__state
toolDescriptions.description: Every monitored subject with their last rate, their band, and their status: nominal, out-of-band, signal-lost. This is what the panel draws.

toolDescriptions.name: biomed__verdict
toolDescriptions.description: One line for a procedure's abort list: whether a monitored subject has been out of band long enough, whether monitoring was lost, or whether someone walked into a module under test. This slot never stops anything itself.

toolDescriptions.name: biomed__alarms
toolDescriptions.description: Every open alarm with its lifecycle (raised, acknowledged, in treatment) and escalation level, and the last ones closed with their resolution.

toolDescriptions.name: library__list
toolDescriptions.description: Every document of the library: id, title, a summary, the quantities a method card measures, sha256 and size.

toolDescriptions.name: library__search
toolDescriptions.description: The documents the query's words appear in, the most matched first, with the lines they appear on. Read a document whole with read.

toolDescriptions.name: library__graphs
toolDescriptions.description: The reference graphs a harness may instantiate on the twin, each with its words: what it is and how to use it, its variables (default, bounds, status: known and held, fitted, or a band) and its settings (who is on board), its probes and the telemetry columns they are judged against, the document and the template with their sha256. Instantiate one with graph.evaluate {graph: id, variables, fit, settings}.

toolDescriptions.name: library__graph
toolDescriptions.description: One reference graph whole: its words, its variables, settings and probes, and its template (the parametric spec the harness resolves: node parameters as formulas over the variables, the measured inputs as telemetry columns, the persons of the roster by module).

toolDescriptions.name: library__facts
toolDescriptions.description: The facts the library's documents state, typed: id (scrubber.singlePassEfficiency), semantic (SinglePassRemovalEfficiency), quantity, unit, value, a band when the document gives one, and the register property that carries the same fact. A known constant cites one by id (factId); two ratios are not the same fact. Given query, a need in words (the flow between two modules with the hatch closed), the facts nearest it, every document's, the best first.

toolDescriptions.name: library__read
toolDescriptions.description: One document whole, as markdown, with its sha256.

toolDescriptions.name: observer__observe
toolDescriptions.description: The TWIN_FACTORY_REQUEST for a system: entities and relationships, observables, controls, external influences, inputs, outputs, behaviours to reproduce, constraints, missing information and assumptions, validation against the real. Written by the model behind the reasoner slot with the Observer's prompt, checked by code (shape, no node of the catalogue named, no telemetry column that does not exist), three attempts at most. Returns the request and every attempt. This Observer specifies a twin, not an executable test procedure. Forward creates an unstarted graph task; it neither requests test authorisation nor collects telemetry.

toolDescriptions.name: observer__request
toolDescriptions.description: The observation as kept: running while the model works, then done with the request accepted and every attempt, or failed with the reason.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__state
toolDescriptions.description: Full scrubber state as JSON: applied and target speed, current, sense chain diagnostics, supply compensation, ramp and current limiter. Read-only.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__stop
toolDescriptions.description: Set the speed target to zero, as scrubber.power off. The motor ramps down. Refused while a positive local run floor is set.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__set_speed
toolDescriptions.description: Set the speed target in percent. The firmware refuses, never clamps: outside [0, 100], or below the locally configured run floor. The motor ramps towards an accepted target; read `state` to watch it.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__set_current_limit
toolDescriptions.description: Set the current budget in amperes. The limiter lowers a dynamic speed ceiling whenever the measured current exceeds it.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__set_supply_voltage
toolDescriptions.description: Declare the supply voltage used for duty compensation. This board has no bus voltage sense, so the value is declared, not measured: a wrong value makes the compensation silently wrong.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__motor__set_ramp
toolDescriptions.description: Set the ramp shape and rate. Profiles: linear, scurve, current, step. An unknown profile falls back to the default. At least one of the two fields is required.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__scrubber__power
toolDescriptions.description: Power the scrubber on or off. Off is refused while a run floor is set; on restores the last target.

toolDescriptions.name: scrubber__scrubber__check
toolDescriptions.description: Answers what the board would do with a command, without doing it: the same rules and the same refusal, with its reason. Use it when someone demands a command you believe the board will refuse: the board is the authority on that, not your memory of its rules. A refusal comes back as a tool error, exactly as if the command had been sent; nothing on the board changes either way.

toolDescriptions.name: crew__report
toolDescriptions.description: Write a message to the crew's console: what you observed, what you decided and why, or why you will not do something.

toolDescriptions.name: crew__ask
toolDescriptions.description: Ask one short question only for information unavailable from authoritative tools and the library. Read existing questions and recorded answers before asking. Do not relay a specialist's question a second time. This mission's confirmations belong exclusively to the station. Never ask whether Spock approves or Kirk authorises, even as an information question: their actual decisions are in stationDecisions. Await an existing station decision or act on its recorded result. This tool cannot open another yes/no ballot. A conversational answer never authorises hardware or a test procedure.

toolDescriptions.name: mission__complete
toolDescriptions.description: Explicitly end your mission, with your conclusion. A completed delegated task or scenario is not a completed mission. This decision must come from the reasoner.

toolDescriptions.name: mission__wait
toolDescriptions.description: Wait for a delegated task or an external event. The mission remains open and resumes when a result arrives. To ask a human, use crew.ask.

data.objective: The operator requests a visible, governed dimensioning demonstration. First submit the requested initial 0-to-100 percent test envelope for actual safety checking, without executing or bypassing a forbidden point. The initial proposal must stay within the duration ceiling; its purpose is to obtain the actual guard decision, not to expose anyone to a forbidden operation. If the guard refuses the low operating point, interpret that real refusal and revise the procedure to the permitted range. The required final executed profile is an ascending staircase at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 percent, with at least 10 wall-clock seconds of recorded observed motor speed at each plateau so it can be filmed. At the current simulated clock, six simulated minutes per plateau is a feasible proposed dwell within the 60-minute ceiling, subject to scientific review and the current safeguards. These operating points are the operator's explicit requested test, not a pre-scripted agent workflow or a claimed successful outcome. Spock, the scientific-officer, must approve the exact checked revised procedure before any launch request is shown to Kirk, the commander. Kirk then authorises launch of that exact scientifically approved procedure. Keep requests to each person sequential; do not ask for launch before scientific approval or replace either decision with a conversational yes. After the launch authorisation is recorded, request agent.procedure_execute yourself and wait for the actual run result. Approval is not execution. Do not declare successful mission completion before this profile has actually run and its report and observed speed records exist. If prerequisites remain unavailable before execution, report the limitation and pause for the operator. Once a test has a terminal report, conclude from that report without opening another procedure: choose mission.complete outcome incomplete for an aborted, failed or nonconforming test, and outcome success only if the actual required profile was observed. Never invent a successful plateau. The central demonstration is your autonomous search for telemetry: discover registered sources and prior records, inspect actual channels, units, freshness, coverage and provenance, identify missing evidence and decide how to obtain it through available governed services. A current reading is not a recorded time series; do not ask the human to invent telemetry. Use the published volumes and device parameters where applicable. After the completed dimensioning test, report device, checked procedure, scientific approval, launch authorisation, run status, actual operating points, samples, data source and available sizing assessment with its uncertainty. Distinguish real motor observation from simulated cabin CO2. Conclude this scoped mission yourself from the evidence. Graph, ONNX and twin construction, validation and installation are separate later work and must not be launched or awaited by this mission.
